title: Policyholder Service Desk Rules: Deferred Fixed Annuities Beneficiary Designations
content:
The owner of an Ashgrove Deferred Fixed Annuities contract names primary and contingent beneficiaries.

## When a designation is recorded

| Condition | Record relied on |
|---|---|
| A beneficiary designation is recorded only while the contract status is applied or active. | The status on this contract's record. |
| A changed designation is recorded only from a beneficiary change request signed by the owner, and, where the current designation names an irrevocable beneficiary, also signed in consent by that beneficiary. | The beneficiary change service request on this contract (its signed date and status) and the designation type of the lines currently in effect. |

## Effect and form of a designation

- The new designation replaces the earlier one entirely, effective on the owner's signature date if signed while the owner was living.
- Shares are whole percents, each at least the tier's smallest beneficiary share, totalling 100 in each class (primary and contingent).
- No more than the tier's maximum number of primary beneficiaries may be named.
- On an IRA contract, where the owner lives in a community property state, the owner's spouse must consent in writing to a primary designation of anyone else.

## Checks on a proposed designation (hypothetical, on a tier with a 1% smallest share and at most 10 primaries)

| Proposed designation | Result |
|---|---|
| Primaries 50% and 50%; contingent 100% | Shares acceptable |
| Primaries 33%, 33%, 33% | Not acceptable — the class totals 99 |
| Primaries 99.5% and 0.5% | Not acceptable — not whole percents, and 0.5% is below 1% |
| Eleven primaries | Not acceptable — more than 10 |
| Change request signed by the owner only, while the current designation names an irrevocable beneficiary | Not recorded — the irrevocable beneficiary's consent signature is required |

**Basis question.** *Does a new designation keep any line of the old one?* No — it replaces the earlier designation entirely.
